name: Blend, in three taps
object: Blend, the Spotify feature that merges one listener's taste with friends into a single shared, auto-updating playlist
audience: existing Spotify users who haven't tried Blend yet and want a fast how-to
message: This video tells existing users that turning their taste and a friend's taste into one shared playlist takes three taps, no setup required.

moments.what: A 'Spotify Tips and Tricks' bumper opens on an abstract graphic of intertwined hands, rendered in Spotify's green-on-blue brand palette.
Bold type over big overlapping green circles states the benefit: seeing what the whole group listens to, in a playlist shared with up to ten friends that refreshes daily.
moments.copy: See what the whole squad is listening to. Share a curated playlist with up to 10 friends, updated daily based on everyone's taste.

moments.what: Three phone-screenshot steps follow in sequence: searching 'Blend' and tapping the top result, selecting 'Create a Blend', then tapping Invite and sending it to a friend.
moments.copy: Search 'Blend' and tap the first result. Select Create a Blend. Tap Invite and send it to friends.

moments.what: A radiating green play-button icon fills the screen, then the video closes on the plain Spotify wordmark.

cta: No spoken or typed 'try it' line — the three demoed steps are the call to action, and the video simply closes on a play icon and the Spotify logo once the Blend has been sent.
why: Framing the whole thing as a 'Tips and Tricks' explainer rather than an ad sets different expectations: it promises to be useful rather than persuasive, which makes the single benefit line up front and the literal three-step demo that follows feel like a favour, not a pitch. Ending on the finished invite rather than a slogan reinforces that the feature itself is the reward.
